text:
Pyotr Kochetkov stopped all 26 shots he faced, and Carolina made sure Winnipeg's nine-game winless slide (0-7-2) got worse in a 7-0 rout at Lenovo Center. Kochetkov, a second-round pick of the Hurricanes in 2019 who was ranked first among international goalies that year, saved 3.2 goals more than the quality of those shots called for. That is goals saved above expected, which measures a goalie against the chances he actually faced. Sean Walker scored twice and took first star.

The game turned in a wild stretch of the second period, when Carolina scored three times in about seven minutes. Juuso Välimäki's slap shot made it 2-0 on a 2% chance, the least likely goal of the night, and Sebastian Aho added a power-play goal 24 seconds later. Walker and Logan Stankoven followed, and it was 5-0 before the period was half gone.

The scoreboard was lopsided, but the play was closer than the score. Carolina's expected goals, a measure of shot quality, were 4.65 to Winnipeg's 3.25, and our simulations of every shot gave the Hurricanes a 70% chance to win, not a certainty. Winnipeg's best look was a 41% chance for Gabriel Vilardi in the second period, and Kochetkov stopped it. Stuart Skinner allowed five goals on 17 shots after Clay Stevenson gave up two on 15.

Carolina has won four straight and beat Winnipeg for the second time this season after a 3-2 win on Oct. 17. The Jets are winless in nine and need an answer quickly.
